chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

The sun's decline was mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: "You take a stick whose length is three ashbar (cubits/handsbreadths), and if it is longer, it is clearer. It is set up, and as long as you see the shadow decreasing, the sun has not declined. When the shadow increases after the decrease, the sun has declined."
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the time of Maghrib is the setting of the sun, until he says: And the time of Fajr.

key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (solar noon transition)

ai.seo_question: How to determine the exact start time of Dhuhr prayer using the sun's shadow?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the practical astronomical method for determining the onset of Dhuhr prayer by observing the shadow of a vertical stick, specifically noting that the time begins when the shadow starts to lengthen after reaching its minimum. While the summary mentions Dhuhr, the text explicitly links this 'Zawal' (decline) to the broader framework of prayer times, concluding with a reference to the time of Fajr, thereby establishing the sun's position as the primary marker for the daily prayer cycle. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise, observable natural signs for religious obligations.
